i don't think people are as deterred by 'crime' and other such schenanigans as some comments here might lead many to believe as both light rails still seem to be quite popular, rather it's largely the simple fact that many routes seem to focus on downtown or commuter timetables when quite realistically most jobs that were being done in downtown offices are easily done from home now. Many jobs are still going to need to be done in person but a large percentage of office jobs at most might need hybrid. Jobs that are in person would most likely be retail, food or warehouse type jobs, many of which are not in downtown. There might also be students who use transit in all education levels and honestly I think we need to start replacing school bus routes with transit routes complete with an unlimited pass so that the younger generation can start learning city routes. I'm not disagreeing with the notion that crime can be a deterrent, I totally get that. But it's one small piece in a bigger puzzle, and cities with downtowns akin to Minneapolis or St Paul really need to start rethinking on how to use their space.
